name: Tanzania
headline: Tanzania: +5.9% growth in 2025, 3.3% inflation, debt 50% of GDP
sections: Tanzania is a $89.6 billion economy (2025), the world's 85th-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew +5.9% in 2025, faster than the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $4,471 at purchasing-power parity (2025), against a world median of $21K. Manufacturing accounts for 8.4% of GDP (2023).
Consumer prices rose 3.3% in 2025, broadly within typical target ranges, down from 4.4% in 2022. Unemployment stood at 1.6% (2025), below the world median of 5.1%. Youth unemployment was 2.4% (2025).
Gross government debt is 50% of GDP (2025), a moderate level that has risen from 41% in 2020. The general government balance is −2.6% of GDP (2025).
The current account balance is −2.6% of GDP (2025). Trade equals 39% of GDP (2025), a relatively closed economy. Net FDI inflows were 1.9% of GDP (2025).
IMF projections put government debt at 41% of GDP by 2031, on a declining path from today's level. Life expectancy is 67.2 years (2024). Population: 70.5 million (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
